 A sign indicating that SNAP benefits are accepted inside a store in Watertown. Jonathon Wheeler/Watertown Daily Times
 WATERTOWN — A city woman was arrested Wednesday on a warrant accusing her of providing false employment and income information to obtain $4,596 in food assistance benefits, according to police and charging documents.
 Tamara Ann Watson, 31, was charged Oct. 28 with first-degree offering a false instrument for filing, third-degree grand larceny, third-degree welfare fraud and misuse of food stamps, all felonies.
